llm.summary: The skill is not malicious, but it needs review because it can run broadly, avoid normal user checkpoints, write task details to a workspace memory file, and send progress details to Telegram.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is autonomous multi-step task execution, and the memory file plus progress updates fit that purpose, but the skill also directs command execution, file creation, data fetching, and external notifications as part of that workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Activation includes explicit Ralph Loop phrases but also 'any task the user expects the AI to execute autonomously without questions,' which is broad and could trigger without a clear opt-in for this specific mode.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains only SKILL.md and _meta.json, with no executable install scripts, dependencies, or package-install behavior. Static scan and VirusTotal supplied no malicious detections.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires sending Telegram messages with task names, progress, blockers, produced files, and workspace paths. That external data flow is purpose-related but sensitive enough that users should explicitly understand and control it.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates and repeatedly updates /workspace/memory/ralph-loop.md, including the user's original request verbatim, then deletes it at completion. This is disclosed, but it may temporarily expose sensitive task details and has limited opt-out or scoping guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an explicitly autonomous workflow. Avoid using it for confidential, regulated, or credential-heavy tasks unless you are comfortable with task metadata being written to the workspace and sent to Telegram, and consider asking the agent to use Ralph Loop only when you say the exact trigger phrase.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The autonomy is central to the skill, but the broad catch-all activation and 'do not ask' posture create a real control and consent concern beyond the named Ralph Loop trigger phrases.
[SQP-2] expected: Telegram progress updates are disclosed and tied to the skill's purpose, but the artifact does not provide opt-in, redaction, or disable guidance for task details and file paths sent to an external channel.
[SQP-2] expected: A temporary workspace memory file is core to the loop design and is disclosed, but storing the original request verbatim and updating it throughout execution can expose sensitive details during the run.
